twinfield boekhouden: Waarom dit artikel: twinfield boekhouden: Why this article? Because business owners often know that their accounting ‘is in Twinfield’, but during the month-end closing or in receivables management they run into the same problems: outstanding invoices that remain unpaid, bank and administrative discrepancies and unclear ownership for corrective actions. Below is an immediately applicable step-by-step plan that connects internal and external signals with strategy, money, processes, people and risks — including who decides, who executes and how you measure the result.
Signalen die je nu moet checken - Openst: Signals you should check now - Outstanding invoices (aging) per customer and per ledger date. - Unmatched bank ledger entries versus bank statement (bank reconciliation). - Items in draft bookings or unclear journals at month-end closing. - External changes: customer payment behaviour, industry cycle or changes in VAT/tax rules that affect your cash flow.
Hoe weet ik of mijn Twinfield-koppeling: How do I know if my Twinfield integration and processes are the real cause? (reader question) - Check question (signal): compare the export of open items from Twinfield with your receivables list in Excel/BI-tool on exact invoice number and balance. - Context: if rows are missing or amounts differ, there is a synchronization or master data problem (customer number/currency/GL mapping). - Consequence if you do nothing: delayed collections, higher DSO and unreliable monthly figures. - Decision: restore the source synchronization or assign ownership for data correction. - Action and owner: Finance-operator (owner) performs the correct customer mapping and repostings; IT/system administration checks integration logs. - Measurement point: 100% match between Twinfield open items and receivables report within 5 working days after month-end closing; deviations recorded and resolved.
Stappenplan: sluit de maand en maak het: Step-by-step plan: close the month and make it reproducible (7-step closed improvement loop) 1) Detect (day 0–3 after month end): export three sources: Twinfield outstanding items, bank transactions and sales invoices. - Owner: Finance-operator. - Outcome metric: exports available and stored in central folder/report. 2) Contextualize (day 1–4): match outstanding items with bank transactions and outstanding sales invoices; note differences (unmatched lines, currency deviations, missing customer codes). - Owner: Business Controller. - Outcome metric: overview of all deviations with priority label (high/med/low). 3) Assess consequences (day 2–5): evaluate cashflow impact and risk (e.g., which customer has >60 days outstanding). - Owner: Finance Manager. - Outcome metric: list of top 10 customers by risk and estimated exposure per customer (qualitative estimate acceptable). 4) Decide (day 3–6): choose actions per deviation: collection action, credit note, rebooking correction, or adjustment of the integration/master data. - Decision owner: CFO or responsible business owner. - Metric: per case a document with decision and deadline. 5) Execute action (day 4–14): operational execution (calls with customer, creating reminders, accounting corrections, IT fix for integration). - Action owner: Accounts Receivable / Finance-operator / IT depending on action. - Metric: status update per case (open/closed/IT ticket). 6) Measure result (month-end + 7 days): measure concrete outcomes: number of closed items, reduction in outstanding value, and reconciliation ratio of bank lines. - Owner: Business Controller. - Metric: reconciliation ratio (number of bank transactions matched / total bank transactions) and percentage of outstanding invoices closed within the horizon. 7) Learn and adjust (monthly review): update procedures, authorizations and integration tests; create fixed dashboards or checks. - Owner: CFO/Finance Lead. - Metric: improved time-to-close (reduction in days to full reconciliation) and fewer recurring errors.
Koppel interne en externe veranderingen: Link internal and external changes to strategy, money, processes, people and risks - Strategy: prioritize customers or products that are strategically important in collection decisions; decide a simple policy for leniency vs. strict collection. - Money: measure direct cashflow impact of non-matches (missed collections) and require monthly cash forecast updates. - Processes: formalize who may correct entries when (authorizations), and build standard reconciliation steps into Twinfield protocols. - People: always assign one owner per discrepancy (no 'unknown'); train employees once per quarter on common integration errors. - Risks: record documentation (chain of evidence) for tax inspections and audit; assess customer credit risks periodically.
Controlevragen en korte audits die je va: Control questions and short audits you can do today - When was the last successful synchronization between Twinfield and your integration partner? Is there an error log? - How many outstanding items exist on exactly the same invoice number but with a different amount between Twinfield and your debtor list? - Which five customers have the highest aging and who is their case owner? - Can you perform a bank reconciliation within 48 hours based on a Twinfield export and the bank statement?
